recs.name: Scalding Old Memories
recs.tag: Bygone recollections are beasts, the pursuers behind you.

lines.x: 11:00 P.M. \ Heavy Rain
Meteor's Dorm Room
Why is it raining so heavily? I'm freezing. Guess I'll turn on the heater.
Hm... How do I adjust the temperature? Do I turn this little round thing... but which way...?
Maybe this will do it? Eh, I really can't wrap my head around these gadgets. I wish we had a fireplace.
Phew, look at the time. I wonder when Mina gets off work. The Medic operators really have it hard. We're roommates, but we almost never see each other.
Meteor, it's me. Sorry to call this late.
Mina? I thought you were working overtime? What's the matter? Did you forget something?
It's Gianna. She's crying her eyes out, and asking for you. None of us can calm her down.
Gianna?! What's the matter? Is she alright? Hang on. I'll get changed and come to Medical right away!
No, no, you got it wrong, Meteor! She's scared of thunder! Oh, slow down. I'll take her there, okay?
O-Okay, Mina. Let me talk to her first.
No problem. Gianna? Meteor wants to talk to you. Here you go.
Meteor, I'm scared! *Sobs*, where are you?
Gianna, don't worry. I'll wait for you here. I'll make you some of that snowy rice milk you like.
There, there, Gianna. Don't cry. We'll go to Meteor's right now.
*Whimpers*... I-I'll be strong, Mina... I'll stop crying.
It's okay. We'll be there soon.
Mina, it's very cold over here. Did you give her a few more layers of clothes?
Of course. Medical has sweaters just for children. It'll keep her warm and comfy.
Make sure she's wearing socks and everything.
Of course, of course. Okay, Meteor, I need to carry Gianna, so I'm gonna hang up now. I'll see you in a moment.
Okay, I'll wait for you here. See you.
How am I supposed to stop worrying when all she ever does is cry?
I guess I'll turn up the heat. We need to keep her warm.
A month ago
Medical Department
Meteor, could you please take care of this girl for the time being? Please!
We found her in the ruins. Her family died shielding her when the ceiling fell, and now... Well... she's the only one left.
Well, I definitely don't mind doing that. It's just... why are you coming to me for this? Aren't there professionals in Medical who are better at babysitting?
Medical has actually been pretty overworked lately. I'm ashamed to say this, but we don't have enough manpower, so you're the only one I can turn to.
Oh, right, one second.
What's this...?
This is her evaluation. The psychologists at Medical are recommending that we have someone stay with her at all times, but I don't have the time myself. *Sigh*.
Oh, really? Alright, I'll stay with her when you're busy. Thankfully, I don't really have much going on lately.
Thanks, Meteor. She's still a kid. It's not easy for someone her age to accept her family's gone... I'm sure she'll get back on her feet quickly with you by her side.
Is that a compliment? Well, thanks. So where is this girl? Can I meet her?
Of course. Come with me. She's in the ward over here.
This is the girl?
Yep.
Hey, Gianna? Have you been a good girl and taken your medicine? I brought a new friend with me today.
I've been a good girl today, Mina... Who is that behind you...?
Who are you, lady?
Gianna, this is Meteor. She'll be helping me take care of you from here on out. You don't need to be scared. She's patient and kind. You'll like her.
Mina... *Sobs*... I... I'll be okay. I know you're busy. I'll be a good girl. You don't have to worry.
*Sigh*, Gianna, you're such a sensible girl, it really tugs at my heartstrings.
Meteor, I still have other things to take care of, so I'm going. I'll leave her to you; I'll be back as soon as I'm done.
See you later, Mina.
Um, Miss... N-Nice to meet you. My name is Gianna, and I'm six!
Uh, little girl, I...
I... I've been taking my medicine, and I'm not picky about food. I-I even learned how to fold roses. Do you like roses? I... I'll give you all of them.
Phew—Ahem, Gianna, is it? Hello, I'm Meteor. You don't have to call me 'Miss' or anything; just Meteor will do.
Meteor...?
I know that... you come looking for Mina a lot... I've seen you before. You talk so gentle... I...
If you want to, you can think of me as a big sister. I've always wanted a little sister.
I... May I really?
Of course.
*Whimpers*...
Meteor, I... *Sobs*...
What's the matter? It's okay. Tell your big sister everything.
I-I can't find my doll!
Ah, I see. Have you talked to Mina about it? Did she help you look?
She's very busy... I can't... can't bother her.
That's okay. How about I go look for it, then?
I don't want to look for it anymore. Don't. Don't go, Meteor. Please... Please don't leave me alone.
I won't go anywhere. It's okay. How about I buy you a new one, then?
*Sobs*... I don't want a new doll! I just want a big sister... S-Stay here with me, Meteor. I don't want to be alone.
Don't worry. I'm not going anywhere. I'm here.
*Sobs*—
I'm here. I'm here. Don't worry. You don't need to be scared anymore.
How come Gianna isn't even wearing socks? Mina, why is she completely barefoot?!
It's not my fault! She said she wanted to come look for you, and she ran out the door after she put on a sweater! I couldn't catch her!
*Whimpers*, Meteor, I'm scared! That boom is too loud! I'm too scared to sleep!
You mean the thunder? Bad, bad thunder. We'll go to the Doctor tomorrow and file a complaint.
Okay, *sobs*...
Okay now, you two come inside.
I'll pass. Here's her toothbrush. Make sure she brushes her teeth after she's done with her milk, and here's her towel, her socks, her hand puppet, and her feather hairpin.
Okay, I got it. Look at you. You're like her mom.
Eh? Now that you mention it, I guess I'm kinda like one. Hm, okay. Gianna? Mommy still has work to do. Be a good girl here, okay?
Come, Gianna, say bye bye to Mina.
*Sobs*... Bye, Mila.
It's Mina, not Mila! Oh, well. I gotta go back. Good night, Meteor.
Good night. I'll see you tomorrow.
*Whimpers*, s-see you tomorrow.
Gianna, you're covered in snot. Don't get my pajamas all dirty, okay?
I won't... *Sniffs*.
You know, I can get you some tissues.
Oh, Meteor, it's coming out again!!
Ahh! Where are the tissues? Right here! Here you go, wipe yourself clean!
Okay now let's tuck you into bed. Be sure to get your feet in too.
Your blanket is so warm, Meteor, and it smells like roses.
*Chuckles*, don't be silly.
Come here, Meteor.
You want a hug?
Yup!
You want me to tell you a story too?
Yup!
Be sure to go to bed after the story, okay? You won't be scared of the thunder anymore, right?
Yeah...
Meteor... Actually, I'm scared because... the same thing happened that day too. Daddy, Mommy, and my big sister all got colder and colder... That's why I'm scared.
I see... You're scared of the thunder because of what happened...?
*Sobs*... I wanna be as strong as you, but I'm not...
It's okay. I get scared because of things that happened in the past too, Gianna.
Really? But you always look like you're not scared of anything. How do you do that?
Well, first I think of the things that I'm scared of as big, scary monsters. Then I imagine myself a brave hunter.
What do you do after that?
Well, this is where I tell you a little story.
A story? What kind?
Once upon a time, in a big forest in faraway Kazimierz, there was a thick pile of leaves on the ground.
Was there something in the pile?
A little hunter, shivering...
Just like me? I'm shaking in your bed.
You're shaking? Hm, you're right. Your feet are so cold.
Come closer. I'll hold you.
Is it still cold?
Nope.
Let's keep going, then.
Our poor little hunter had left home, and she was lost in the forest, all alone. The chilly wind was seeping through her thin clothes, and her hair was completely drenched by the cold rain.
The sounds of the thunder in the skies high up above were just as loud as the howls of her hungry tummy.
That sounds so scary.
No, what's even scarier is that there was a huge, crafty wild beast following the hunter's weak scent, tracking her down.
It buried its nose in the wet mud and rubbed itself against the coarse tree barks. The bushes, the swamps, the streams. It wasn't going to leave any corner untouched.
Finally, under a dead tree, it finally found it... It found... a foot—!
Ahh! Meteor, you meanie! Let go of my leg!
Yep, looks like your feet aren't so cold anymore.
Hmph, I'm putting my feet on your tummy.
Sure thing. Hm, where were we again?
The beast found her, and it was going to catch her.
Oh, right. The little hunter was so scared that she was hiding in a pile of leaves. She could already hear the beast's breath and the sounds of its hooves trudging through the mud.
Huff—Huff—
*Thump*—
The little hunter was too scared to even breathe. Tears dripped down her face one after another.
The beast had been hunting the hunter day after day, night after night. She managed to get away so many times, but our poor little hunter wasn't going to get away this time.
Don't give up, hunter!
Right, she can't give up! As soon as the beast bore its fangs, the hunter forced herself to calm down and asked, 'Do I really have my back to the wall?'
She held her breath and took out the very last arrow in her quiver. She finally found the courage to take on the beast, looking straight at it through the gaps in the pile of leaves.
Why wasn't she scared anymore?
She remembered a song that her grandpa used to sing for her.
What kind of a song is that? Can you sing it for me, Meteor?

When the little hunter was still a tiny little baby hunter, her grandpa always sang this while he held her: '♪My baby girl, should you find yourself chased through the woods by a beast most vile, under the calm, gentle moon in the sky♪'
'♪Never forget, walk forth in big strides. If there is no way to go, turn around not with fright. With your bow and arrow you must fight, and the beast you must smite♪'

At that moment, the moonlight lit the way, and the earth helped her lift her shoulders. The little hunter released her bowstring, and the roaring breeze sent her arrow straight into the beast's chest, felling it.
Meteor, did the beast die?

Yes, it did. With that tiny bit of determination and courage, the little hunter defeated the frightening beast in the most decisive moment. And me, that's also how I overcame my past, the past that I used to be scared of.
And as long as you can muster up the courage, Gianna, you can overcome anything that—
But, Meteor, I-I don't want to defeat my past! When I'm scared, it's not just the bad things that I remember. I remember all the happy memories I had with everyone too!
Doesn't thinking about them make your heart ache, though?
Yup... it does, and it makes me cry, but it warms up my heart too. When I didn't have you, it was the memories that helped me through everything.
Hmm... really? Looks like... Looks like your little beast doesn't actually want to eat you. Haha.
I don't think the beast in your story wanted to eat the hunter either.
Hm? What makes you think that?
How does the hunter know the beast wants to eat her? She didn't ask the beast, and she's only ever run away. She never tried to talk to the beast.
Well, the beast has been chasing the hunter. What else could it be after, if not eating her?
No, Meteor. You said the hunter was scared, cold, and hungry. You never said she was hurt because the beast chased her.
Maybe it thinks the lonely girl needs a friend to help her out of that place.
Please, Meteor. Please don't kill it.
Meteor? W-What's the matter? Why are you so quiet?
Did I say something wrong?
No, you reminded me of something, in the past.
Is it a memory that makes your chest burn?
Yep, it always makes me feel down in the dumps whenever I think about it. That's why I try my best to keep myself from remembering it.
You can't do that, Meteor.
Yeah, you're right. The hunter was wrong, and I was too. I shouldn't have killed it, and I shouldn't have sealed the memory away.
All those nights I spent in the wastes, away from my family. The pain, the joy, the sorrow, and the boredom... It was there every moment, and it wasn't there to kill me.
(I kind of know what Meteor's saying... but also kind of don't.)
(Deep breath)
Gianna, I... I just came up with a new ending. Wanna hear it?
Yes!
Okay, then. Lie down and get in bed.
I lied down! My eyes are shut, too! Tell me the story!
At the very end, the little hunter took her dagger out, but she didn't use it to stab the beast's heart.
Instead, she cut off a piece of her clothes and bandaged the beast's wound.
She petted the beast's fluffy head and then asked, 'Can you move, buddy?'
The beast pondered a little in silence and then stood up.
Then, she asked the beast, 'I'm going on an adventure. I don't know what lies ahead, but I know I'll need a buddy. Do you want to come?'
The beast didn't stay quiet this time. It neighed happily, and it started to sway its tail from side to side, like a whip.
It ran really fast, and when she rode on its back, it was just like the hunter could grasp the wind.
She wasn't lonely any more. Together, they ran off toward the sunlight.
Zzz—Meteor... I'm tired.
Zzzz—
Are you asleep?
Zzzzz...
Mina's such a dummy.
She thinks you aren't strong enough, but you figured out how to confront those things a long time ago.
(Kisses) But thanks, Gianna.
Thanks...

recs.name: Dilemma
recs.tag: The moons aren't always consummate, and the world has many a shortcoming.

lines.x: Good hustle these past few days, everybody. Let's break a bit early today—we're still twenty-five klicks out from the objective. If we make good time tomorrow morning, I think we'll get there by the afternoon.
Thanks, Meteor. I thought we'd be gnawing on rations in the field. I didn't expect we'd get proper hot meals.
Yeah, never knew you were such a good cook.
So what's stewing today? It smells great, I caught a whiff of it while I was pegging the tents.
It's a hometown specialty.
A secret family recipe?
Nah, I lost my parents when I was very young. It was a village household by the mountains that helped me grow. They're all good and kind people.
This soup is something they taught me. It's simple to make, and good for cooking out in the wilds.
Ah... sorry I brought it up.
What's to be sorry for? It's alright.
Oh, it smells amazing. Can I ask for the recipe?
Of course. It's not complicated.

You need spinach roots and wild gingerflax I just took the chance to dig up, the striped scalecis we caught this afternoon, and I used some pickled jerky and salt I brought along to season, then let it stew for fifteen minutes. Then you're good to go.
So this is what everyone meant when they said we wouldn't regret going with you.
Hardly, I just know a few simple country dishes. I could never compare to a chef like Matterhorn.

Phew. Though, if I could, adding a pinch of staricitron seeds would've made it even better. There's a little spicy kick to them. Drinking some hot meat soup peppered with them can really brush the cold away on days like these.
Staricitron...? It rings a bell, I've heard of a rare tree with the same name. I think it's a wood that a lot of nobles love for furniture.
Ah, and I remember it's a species unique to Kazimierz.
*Sigh*...
Meteor, your home is in Kazimierz. If you've seen them before, why not tell us a little about them.
Right, we really want to know more about where you came from.
Meteor? Meteor, why are you so quiet?
Hm?! Ah, my home...
I've been away for so long. Just what were they like...
It's not coming to me straight away.
Aw, that's a shame—hey! What are you hitting me for?
Eat up, kiddo, or you won't grow any taller.
Do you see this, Meteor?!
Alright, alright, it's getting late. Pour another bowl. I brought some of Matterhorn's crackers too. You can all share them.
Wow, that's incredible! Thanks, Meteor.
Turn in as soon as you're done. I'm a little tired. I'll be going to sleep first.
Where am I? It's so dark.
Meteor, Meteor.
Who is it?
Come quick, Meteor. I've been waiting for you forever.
Who are you?
Meteor, come with me. There's going to be a moonshadow in the sky tonight. We can climb the staricitron tree and see the twin moons.
Lana? What are you doing here?
I've been waiting for you here all this time.
Listen. The wind passing through the damp leaves. It's been pushing me on.
Wind? There's no wind here, Lana. Come here, quick. Don't leave this place.
I'm going, Meteor. Quick, follow me...
Come back, Lana! Where are you going?
Come quick, Meteor. You know I'm waiting for you.
She's... gone.
Meteor! Meteor!
Um... Uncle, why are you here...?
No, never mind. That's right, have you seen Lana? She just came by, and I don't know where she ran off to.
You're mixed up. Lana's been sick for a month now. How's she going outside?
She's sick?! But just now, I swear she was... this is strange... um, how is she, then? Is she any better?
*Sigh* Not much to cheer for. Barely gets her porridge down her in the morning, and she sicks up half a bowl of pink.
How could that be! What about a doctor, then, Uncle? Has a doctor seen her?!
Meteor, it's... why I came to see you today. We've got no real options left now. This winter's gone on too long, autumn was too short. Not a thing left over.
Whole host of the village children are already beyond sickly. If we can't get any more medicine for Lana, she won't be able to make it through the winter.
I still have a bit of savings! I'll give you all of—

...Meteor, it's not enough... there's a man who passed by and said, he wants some staricitron wood. He gets the timber, he'll leave us some money and supplies. We can pull through the winter with those.
Does he have to have those staricitron trees? Countless generations of my family's looked after that forest.
What about other trees, will other trees do? I'm begging you. Just wait a little longer, and we might have some other way. We will...
No, Meteor, we... don't. We love them just as much as you do, but...
Help me, Meteor—*cough* *cough*—we've got no other way.
Meteor, save me!
Meteor—save an old girl!
Meteor, Meteor!
Ah—ahh, ahh! I'll save you all, I will—*huff* *huff*—*urk*—
Meteor, what's wrong? It was a nightmare, wasn't it? It's okay, it's okay, we're all here.
We are. Meteor, want some water? I'll pour you a cup.
Haagh—it's you. I thought...
The pressure of the rescue mission probably got too much. Here, Meteor, wipe that sweat off.
It's alright. Thank you both. My nerves must be taut, running all this way for days. I'm a little worn out.
Meteor, if you want to tell us anything, feel free. We'll help however we can.
It really is alright. We all still need to be on our way. Let's get our things packed and go. I'll be fine.
Meteor!
(Shaking head) Leave it, Keira. Don't ask.
Ah Fêng, how far are we from the objective?
Not far now. Less than three kilometers left—
Oh, crap. Meteor, look. In the direction of the objective.
That's intensely thick smoke. The report didn't mention anything about a fire.
Keira, go look for survivors in the neighboring villages, and band them together to put the fire out! Ah Fêng, get the medicals ready! People have to be hurt with a fire this big! Quick!
On it. Meteor, what about you?
I'll look closer to the scene, and see if I can find any other survivors!
You be careful, then, Meteor!
I will! Keep yourselves safe too!
(The fire's burning too intensely. I can't tell if there's still anyone inside.)
Is anyone there? If you can hear me, please answer me! Is anyone there!
Is anyone there? If you can hear me, please answer me! Is anyone there!
Is-Is that you, Meteor? Get away!
What's going on? Uncle, I just heard a massive explosion come from here, and I ran right over.
Run, quick! Don't come near. Those tree-felling Originium engines the knight-lord brought in exploded. There's Originium dust scattered all over here.
Uncle, just save your voice for now. I'll bind the wound for you. Who else is here?
No, no, you listen to me, Meteor. Get away, quick. You don't go, you won't make it. Those machines might explode again at any time. You... you'll catch ill! Quick, get away from here!
Uncle, I—I can't leave you all behind. Hang in there. I'll bring you out now.
Argh! My eyes—it hurts!
My leg! My leg's gone! Urgh—save me, save my soul!
(What do I do, what do I do, what do I do? Dammit, what should I be doing?!)
What are you still gazing off for? Get out of here. It's dangerous!
Huh—?
*cough* *cough* *cough*—my throat... ghaagh—*cough* *cough* *cough*...
(The back of my hand's... bloody. Did I cut it?)
Uncle! Uncle, are you still alright? Un... cle... are you all...
Answer me! Agh—*cough* *cough*—answer me... *urk*.
Me... teor... come here...
Oh, Uncle! Go on, I'm listening!
We're—*cough* *cough*... all so sorry for you... but Lana... she asked you...
Uncle! Uncle!
How could this happen?
How is everything I do wrong? How is everything I do useless...?
How...
By all rights, her face should be scorched dry by the blistering air, yet Meteor feels wet droplets, rolling down.
(Rubs back of hand against cheek)
Ugh—dammit, I can't believe I'm remembering that at a time like this.
Ohhhh, my child...
(What's that noise? Is there someone crying?)
Ohhh, my child! You wretch, why save me? You should've left me to die, how could you not save our child?!
Darling, it's my fault, I couldn't save our girl... ohh, my precious baby, Daddy's so sorry... *sobbing*
Why are you still here? Get out of here, quick!
Go? How? We can't go a step more. Our whole lives are ruined here... ohhh...
Miss. My leg's hurt. I can't walk. Get my wife out of here, forget about me. Quick, move!
I'm not going—*sobbing*—We're together as a family, and we'll die as a family. Ohhh, my child.
What's happening? Is there still someone inside?
Yes—*sobbing*—my girl's still in there. We were in a rush, and I—I was only in time to rescue my wife, and I left—the disgrace I am, I left my child in there... *sobbing*
Okay, sir. Save your breath. Do you still remember which part of the house your child was in?
You won't be time—the fire's too big. Get my wife out of here. It's all hopeless.
(Grasps the man's collar) Where is she?!
In her bedroom—s—southmost part of the attic.
Got it. Look after your lady.
Watch out—
*cough* *cough*...
Darling? Darling, what's wrong? Someone, anyone! Save her!
(It's all burning too fast. My eyes hurt so much.)
Little girl, can you hear me? *cough* *cough* *cough*....
(South of the attic... oh, there!)
Agh, hot—*cough* *cough*.
(Can only kick it open.)
(I can't see anything clear. Dammit, all this thick smoke.)
Is anyone there? *cough* *cough*—
Save... help me...
(That voice came from the wardrobe!)
I've found you. Oh, thank goodness.
Daddy... mo...
She's losing consciousness already. Hold on, I'll take you away from here.
(Lifts up the girl)
Only when Meteor looks back does she realize the way she came has now been engulfed by the inferno.

The scarlet blaze trails along the walls, stairs and doorframe as it spreads, the searing licks roiling and twisting without end, attempting to charge for the two in the room, lapping at their clothes and skin.
(Agh, now what do I do?!)
Dammit—it's collapsing!
*cough* *cough* *cough*—*hiss*, *huff*—
(I think my back got struck. It hurts. Right, the child!)
(Phew... wonderful, she's alright. No, I need to think of a way to get out fast, I need to get up.)
Argh, it really does hurt.
H-Help... me...
I'll help you, I'll help you, I absolutely will.
(Looks all around)
(There's a gap there. I think I can climb through. It should be from when the wall fell in the collapse just now.)
(This hole is too small, I can't make it in. I can only get the child through first.)
Meteor, are you there?! *cough* *cough* *cough* Where are you?
Keira!!
Is that Keira?! I'm in here, I'm in here! South, there's a small hole here!
Meteor! Ah, I see you! How'll we get through a hole this small? What now? *whimper*
Don't cry, don't mind me for now. The child, get the child away!
Meteor!
Grab onto the child, careful of any splinters.
What about you then, Meteor?! I'll go find Fêng, you wait for me, hold on—
Listen, forget about me, you won't make it. Get the child away quick. Go.
Meteor, no, I can't do that, I'll find some way. We can definitely make it back together. Eargh—
Eek—no, it's too heavy, Keira, we can't push it apart!
We'll try again! Hold onto my hand, and don't let go, Meteor!
Quickly, go! Or else you'll be in danger too!
Damn it all, get the child out of here!!
Meteor!!!!
Meteor...
Lana... I've been waiting for so long...
(Shakes head)
I'm sorry.
Why?
I couldn't save you, and I couldn't save everyone. In the end... I couldn't protect a single thing...
No, you've already done so well. It's enough, now... it's enough.
Were you waiting for me to go with you?
No. I came to say goodbye.
Goodbye?
(Hugging) I'm leaving, Meteor. Don't come with me.
You're going, in the end?
Yes. Don't cry. You're the bravest little hunter. You've still got such a long road to walk, and still so many people who need you.
I miss you, so much. I really do.
I miss you too, but it's time now. Go on, let me go.
See you...
Meteor, you're awake. How do you feel?
Mi...
Making it out alive with injuries as serious as that, it's nothing short of a miracle.
You'd better not pull this next time, heading on missions without any regard for your own safety. Both me and Gianna were worried sick about you.
Pfffheh.
Agh! That hurts.
What are you laughing about?! You've got burns all over your back, your windpipe's burnt, you have a fracture in your spinal column... do you want me to keep tallying for you?
I thought... you'd be crying your... eyes out over me—*cough* *cough*!
What, is that the kind of person I am to you?
Oof... *huff*. Sorry, Mina, for causing you and all of the Medical such hassle.
What are you being guilty for? We're just doing our jobs.
Hfff—Well, I'm sorry, but I'm powerless to promise you that.
You—
Medical gave everything they had to pull you from the cold hands of death this time, but IF there's a next time, we'll all be powerless to promise anything.
I... couldn't just look on as it all happened. I... don't ever want to see people stuck in those circumstances again, truly.
Between a rock and a hard place.
Not one person should ever be forced to make such a choice, forced to part, forced through... loss.
I can't do it, it's just... I can't.
Meteor, are you still brooding on the past?
I knew it, I can't hide anything from you.
At the time, I believed if I just sacrificed the forest I always protected, I'd get to have Lana back, have everyone in the village living peacefully again.
But fate really was too voracious. What it wanted wasn't just my concession.
I gave it an inch, and it wanted a mile, until it stripped my pockets bare of anything left.
We've chatted about this before. Holding onto the past without letting go doesn't solve anything.
You're right. And it's not like I don't understand.
After Lana passed from illness, I took up her bow, and left the forest together with the other Oripathy sufferers.
In those days wandering, I spent ages in a muddle. I hated that noble who refused to shoulder any blame, and left with nothing but a pat on the buttocks.
And I hated myself, powerless to protect my loved ones, the things I cherished.
But when I first met you, you were nothing like that. What happened?
I suppose I saw more, and my outlook changed.
